thread:
cheng: heads-up — a customer reported burst credits getting double-charged when their client disconnects mid-stream and immediately reconnects. looks like partial-token accounting + reconnect resume path are stepping on each other. anyone seen this in prod? :thinking:

joel: saw one error report yesterday, +1. iirc we currently charge on every chunk emitted and never hold a reservation for in-flight streams. if client reconnects and we replay some tokens we end up charging twice.

maria: is the resume token canonical here? what if they reconnect with a different API key (mobile/desktop split) — which account gets billed?

cheng: good q. current behavior: per-key charge at emission time. resume is best-effort; we accept resume token but billing uses the key on the reconnect. so double-charge is possible.

joel: that explains it. longer-term i'd prefer hierarchical enforcement (per-key counters plus per-org ceiling) — but immediate fix should avoid double-billing on resume.

maria: suggestion: server-side ephemeral lease for in-flight tokens. on stream start/resume we create lease with estimated remaining tokens and block that amount in the org/key quota. if reconnect resumes the same lease id we reconcile and either release leftover or finalize charge. if lease TTL expires we finalize charge.

cheng: exactly what i sketched a minute ago. rough algorithm:

```
# on stream start/resume
lease = CreateLease(session_id, estimated_remaining_tokens, ttl=30s)
ReserveQuota(key_or_org, lease.amount, lease.id)
# on chunk emission
Emit(token_chunk) -> increment usage immediately but mark as `provisional` tied to lease
# on successful stream end or resume ack
FinalizeLease(lease.id): convert provisional -> committed, refund reserve - committed
# on lease TTL expiry
FinalizeLease(lease.id) with best-effort reconciliation
```

cheng: key points: lease id must be embedded in stream metadata so reconnects can present it; also record last_ack_seq from client to avoid replaying already-charged tokens.

maria: edge case: two clients concurrently try to resume same session with different keys — we should detect key mismatch and deny second resume or require org-level reconciliation. that needs a policy: prefer original key, or prefer org owner, or refuse.

joel: prefer original key for simplicity. if org-owner wants cross-key resume we can add opt-in in console.

sree: telemetry checklist: we need metrics and traces to make this observable. e.g. `streaming.leases.created`, `streaming.leases.finalized`, `streaming.leases.refunded`, `streaming.partial_tokens.duplicate_charges`. log tags: lease_id, session_id, resume_token, request_id, org_id, key_id. add a dashboard tile showing "in-flight committed tokens" per-org and alerts when > X% of org quota is in-flight.

hana: console UX idea: show a "Streaming commitments" widget next to quota usage that shows current reserved vs consumed vs refunded (time-series). allow clicking into a session to see event timeline (lease created, chunks emitted, resume attempts). this helps SRE/support debug billing disputes.

quota-bot: [quota] Warning — org:acme-inc has 12k in-flight streaming reservations (85% of monthly burst buffer).

maria: tests: add unit tests for double-resume, cross-key-resume, lease TTL finalize, and cases where client never reconnects (refund path). also add e2e test with simulated disconnect/reconnect under load to validate race windows.

joel: deployment plan: small canary on runtime with `lease` off by default. enable for 5% of traffic and monitor `streaming.partial_tokens.duplicate_charges`. if stable, flip on by org via console and then global rollout.

cheng: i'll open a PR that adds lease plumbing + metrics + minimal console exposure (read-only widget). tagging @joel for runtime review and @sree for telemetry. i'll include migration notes and a script to reconcile historical suspected double-billing cases.

hana: thanks — please include a short blameless note for support so they can triage billing tickets quickly.

cheng: will do. next steps: PR + canary + dashboard alert.
